elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added operative language permits Customer to terminate “this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Customer may terminate on “thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor.”

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 10.2 requires Vendor to refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after any termination, which includes Customer's convenience termination and operates as a pro-rata refund for the post-termination period.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly states that Vendor has no right to terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause requires 30 days' notice, not notice within the specified 60-to-90-day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed, so the conditional cap requirement is satisfied.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: No affirmative Vendor convenience-termination right is granted, and Vendor is expressly barred from exercising such a right during a committed term; this is at least as restrictive as allowing termination only at term end.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No operative Vendor convenience-termination right exists, so a Vendor convenience termination that could trigger the notice duty is demonstrably absent.
